records.Entity / project type: hosted crypto payment processor with major Bitcoin lineage
records.Concise description: Long-running hosted payment processor that accepts Bitcoin alongside other digital assets and provides merchant checkout, integrations, invoicing and settlement.
records.Deeper researched summary: BitPay was one of Bitcoin's earliest major merchant processors and remains active as a broader crypto payments company. Its merchant model intermediates checkout and settlement rather than delivering each payment directly to a merchant-controlled Bitcoin address; businesses can choose supported fiat or crypto settlement configurations. Current support material continues to list both Bitcoin on-chain and Lightning payment acceptance.
records.Launch / history: Founded in 2011, BitPay became a formative Bitcoin merchant processor before expanding into a multi-asset payments business.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It materially explains the evolution from early hosted Bitcoin merchant processing to modern multi-rail crypto checkout and remains important enough to include despite its broader crypto scope.
Important technical or cultural characte: Merchant invoicing, plugins and API integrations
records.Verification basis: Current official business/developer materials and 2026 merchant support verify active operation and Bitcoin/Lightning acceptance; its 2011 launch history is well established.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not present BitPay as Bitcoin-only.
Settlement currencies, merchant eligibility and fees are time-sensitive.
BIP70 belongs in a separate historical standards profile rather than being treated as BitPay's current Bitcoin payment requirement.

records.Concise description: Bitcoin-focused merchant service offering cloud point of sale and checkout/API tooling for Lightning and on-chain payments with BTC delivery or optional fiat conversion.
records.Deeper researched summary: Swiss Bitcoin Pay is designed around merchant acceptance rather than a general consumer wallet. Its current product describes a web/cloud terminal, dashboard and checkout API, with Bitcoin automatically delivered to a merchant private wallet in the BTC-settlement model and optional fiat conversion where supported. This makes the custody distinction important: direct BTC delivery can preserve merchant key control, while conversion and hosted service functions introduce processor dependencies.
records.Launch / history: Developed as a Bitcoin-first merchant acceptance service with point-of-sale and ecommerce tooling.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: It provides a useful middle model between a fully self-hosted server and a traditional custodial processor: hosted merchant tooling can still settle BTC to a merchant-controlled wallet.
Important technical or cultural characte: BTC settlement to merchant private wallet in supported configuration
Hosted service dependency despite self-custody BTC destination
records.Verification basis: Current official product and API material verifies active Lightning/on-chain merchant acceptance and merchant wallet settlement options.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not generalize the service as globally non-custodial: fiat conversion and hosted service dependencies have different trust assumptions.
Fees and jurisdiction availability are time-sensitive.

records.Concise description: Merchant payment orchestration software that creates invoices and checkout flows while routing Bitcoin or Lightning payments directly to a merchant's connected wallet or provider.
records.Deeper researched summary: Zaprite explicitly distinguishes itself from a payment processor: it says it does not hold or process merchant funds. Merchants connect payment destinations, and Zaprite provides checkout, invoicing, API/webhooks and accounting-oriented workflow. A connected destination can itself be self-custodial or custodial, so Zaprite's non-custodial orchestration layer should not be used to infer the custody model of every end-to-end payment.
records.Launch / history: Launched in the early 2020s as Bitcoin-focused invoicing and payment coordination software and continued to ship product updates through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: Zaprite shows that merchant payment UX, invoicing and reconciliation can be separated from custody and payment processing itself.
Important technical or cultural characte: Does not take custody of funds
Can coordinate non-Bitcoin payment methods without changing its Bitcoin-focused role
records.Verification basis: Current official website, support material and 2026 release activity verify active operation and the explicit 'not a processor / never touches funds' model.
Research notes / uncertainties: The connected wallet or payment provider may be custodial; do not label the entire end-to-end merchant flow self-custodial solely because Zaprite does not take custody.

records.Concise description: Lightning-focused merchant acceptance service with point-of-sale, ecommerce and gateway tooling plus BTC or supported fiat settlement paths.
records.Deeper researched summary: IBEX Pay provides retail and ecommerce Lightning acceptance and promotes API/plugin integration, with product material also describing on-chain Bitcoin paths for some flows. Merchant BTC settlement can be directed to a supplied Bitcoin wallet, while fiat conversion requires IBEX and regulated/payment partners. The product remains reachable and commercially positioned, but some public regional/settlement material is not clearly dated, so current geography and fiat support should not be treated as timeless.
records.Launch / history: Developed as a Bitcoin/Lightning merchant and payments business with a strong focus on retail acceptance.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin payments e: IBEX Pay is a meaningful example of merchant-facing Lightning infrastructure combining POS UX with optional conversion rather than simply exposing a node API.
Important technical or cultural characte: Some on-chain support described in first-party material
records.Verification basis: Current first-party product surface verifies active merchant acceptance, but a portion of jurisdiction, fiat-settlement and product-detail documentation appears inconsistently dated, supporting MEDIUM rather than HIGH confidence.
Research notes / uncertainties: Reverify exact supported countries, fiat conversion regions, fees and payment thresholds immediately before any public profile.
Do not imply all IBEX Pay flows are non-custodial; custody/trust differs between BTC-wallet settlement and fiat conversion.
